## Claims
- [proved] For \(a\ge0\), \(0\le b\le j\), and \(\rho\subseteq b^a\),
\[
 \sum_{\sigma\subseteq\rho}(-1)^{|\rho|-|\sigma|}
 \omega(s_{\rho/\sigma})s_{(i^j,\sigma)}
 =(-1)^{|\rho|}s_{(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{j-b})}.
\]
- [proved] The identity remains valid for \(\rho=\varnothing\), for \(a=0\), and for \(b=j\).
- [proved] Applying \(\Lambda\to A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), and then \(J_v\to J_v/A_+J_v\), preserves the established identity.

## Strategy
Put \(h_d=0\) for \(d<0\), \(h_0=1\).  For \(\tau=(\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_m)\), Jacobi–Trudi is
\[
s_\tau=\det\bigl(h_{\tau_u-u+v}\bigr)_{1\le u,v\le m}.
\tag{JT}
\]
Pad \(\rho,\sigma\) to \(a\) parts and \(\rho',\sigma'\) to \(b\) parts.  Thus
\[
s_{(i^j,\sigma)}
=\det\begin{pmatrix}
(h_{i-u+v})_{\substack{1\le u\le j\\1\le v\le j+a}}\\[1mm]
(h_{\sigma_u-j-u+v})_{\substack{1\le u\le a\\1\le v\le j+a}}
\end{pmatrix},
\tag{1}
\]
while
\[
\omega(s_{\rho/\sigma})=s_{\rho'/\sigma'}
=\det\bigl(h_{\rho'_u-\sigma'_v-u+v}\bigr)_{1\le u,v\le b}.
\tag{2}
\]

The bordered Jacobi–Trudi Laplace expansion is
\[
\det\bigl(h_{\lambda_u-u+v}\bigr)_{1\le u,v\le j},
\quad
\lambda=(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{j-b}),
\]
\[
=(-1)^{|\rho|}
 \sum_{\sigma\subseteq\rho}
 (-1)^{|\sigma|}
 \det\bigl(h_{\rho'_u-\sigma'_v-u+v}\bigr)_{u,v=1}^{b}
 \det\begin{pmatrix}
(h_{i-u+v})_{\substack{1\le u\le j\\1\le v\le j+a}}\\
(h_{\sigma_u-j-u+v})_{\substack{1\le u\le a\\1\le v\le j+a}}
\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{3}
\]
Here the Laplace minors are indexed by \(\sigma\subseteq\rho\).  Explicitly, the boundary path of \(\sigma\) is encoded by
\[
I_\sigma=\{\sigma'_{b+1-u}+u:1\le u\le b\}\subseteq\{1,\ldots,a+b\},
\]
and
\[
\sum_{x\in I_\sigma}x=|\sigma|+\binom{b+1}{2}.
\]
Thus the ordinary Laplace sign relative to the empty-path minor is
\[
(-1)^{\sum I_\sigma-\sum I_\varnothing}=(-1)^{|\sigma|}.
\]
The fixed border contributes \((-1)^{|\rho|}\); hence the total coefficient is
\[
(-1)^{|\rho|+|\sigma|}
=(-1)^{|\rho|-|\sigma|}.
\]
This is the complete sign in (3); no further sign is introduced by (JT).

Substituting (1) and (2) into (3) gives exactly
\[
(-1)^{|\rho|}
s_{(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{j-b})}
=
\sum_{\sigma\subseteq\rho}(-1)^{|\rho|-|\sigma|}
\omega(s_{\rho/\sigma})s_{(i^j,\sigma)}.
\]

For \(\rho=\varnothing\), only \(\sigma=\varnothing\) occurs, and both sides are \(s_{i^j}\). If \(a=0\), necessarily \(\rho=\varnothing\), so this same calculation applies. If \(b=j\), the trailing block \(i^{j-b}=i^0\) is empty, and (JT) is the \(j\times j\) determinant for \((i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_j)\).

Finally, quotienting the identity in \(\Lambda\) gives
\[
\sum_{\sigma\subseteq\rho}(-1)^{|\rho|-|\sigma|}
\overline{\omega(s_{\rho/\sigma})}\,\overline{s}_{(i^j,\sigma)}
=(-1)^{|\rho|}\overline{s}_{(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{j-b})}
\quad\text{in }A,
\]
and its image is the identical equality in \(J_v/A_+J_v\).

## Gaps
None for the stated determinant identity.
